applied.summary: `agent_end` cost fields had no unit; INV-3 makes the budget guard read them. Bound to integer micro-dollars (µ$) per DD-9, explicitly excluding float dollars and `costCents`.

`contextWindow` was a widened-contract field with no resolution source and no defined unknown value, and the Infra row attributed its validation to DF1.5 — a phantom dependency (R5 §2 lists DF1.2 only). Now resolves from the DF1.1 roster entry, `0` = unknown-never-full, with DF1.5 named as a later hardening and explicitly not a dependency.

INV-1 asserted `retries` outside `0..5` is rejected at construction, but no AC or test covered it — the one configuration that defeats the story's entire bounded-loop premise was unverified. Added to make-or-break AC1 and to the send-count-matrix DoD test (`retries: 6` / `-1` rejected, not clamped).

AC3 said a turn reporting `aborted`/`error` must not overwrite occupancy without naming the field, while the DoD test used `stopReason`. Unified on `stopReason: aborted | error` (R4 §1.10, `MOD/agent_pi.py:272-275`).

AC1 phrased `PARSE_FIX_ATTEMPTS` as a per-phase param alongside `retries`, contradicting Technical Notes (module constant = 2) and weakening INV-1's no-configuration-raises-the-ceiling claim. Reworded to distinguish phase param from module constant.

Observability contract logged `exitStatus` on a failed trace write. That is the CC-1 5-value run-classification enum (`cli-anything/src/types.ts:79`); a failed SQLite insert is none of its values — carried through unfiltered from the R1 template boilerplate. Replaced with `statement` and an explicit note that the enum classifies a terminated run, not an insert.

`sessions.archived` was declared with no writer, and INV-3 (exactly one writable connection, owned by the tracer; all readers `{readonly:true}`) forbids its only known writer — DF4.1's archive route, the visualizer's single write (R4 §2.5). Column now specified as review-triage never written by a run, with DF4.1 archiving through the tracer's connection rather than opening its own.

Migration checklist (chain-linearizability / cross-story collision): the flat MIGRATIONS list had no ordering or ownership rule while DF1.8 also adds trace columns. Declared append-only and order-stable, later stories append and never edit or reorder.

Migration checklist (lock-acquisition risk): `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` runs at init holding the writer lock against `busy_timeout=5000`, with no constraint on the decls. Every `decl` now required nullable or constant-default so each ALTER is metadata-only.

INV-1 (F11 confidentiality) set modes on 'the file' only, but the WAL `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars carry the same compiled prompts, and a harvest copying `trace.db` without a checkpoint copies an incomplete db into the DF2.5 harvest set. Sidecars now named in-boundary with `0600`, and harvests checkpoint the WAL first.
`sessions.total_cost` — the persisted mirror of DF1.3's `agent_end` cost — carried no unit, the exact gap DD-9 exists to close. Bound to integer micro-dollars (µ$).

`sessions.pipeline_name` had no stated mapping to SSSF's `adw_name` (R4 §2.1 MIGRATIONS list), leaving rename-vs-net-new ambiguous; and migration checklist 'column rename dual-write' was unaddressed. Mapping stated, and the `adw_id`→`request_id` change explicitly scoped as a port-time rename in a schema this repo never shipped under the old name — no live-column rename path exists.

'Signal handling is DF1.1's; this story provides the `processes_end_all` it calls' read as a predecessor calling a successor's function. Reworded: DF1.1 owns the handler, DF1.4 ships the function that handler and `session_finish` both call.

surviving.summary: `events.tokens` has no stated relationship to `sessions.total_tokens` — whether it is a per-event slice rolled up into the session total, and when that rollup is computed, is inferable but unspecified.
`sessions.status` has no enumerated value domain, unlike `phases.status` which carries an explicit `DEFAULT 'fail'` and a stated must-be-earned semantic.
`UsageBreakdown`'s field list is relied on (input excludes cache reads; `reasoningTokens` nested under output) but never enumerated in-story — it is reachable only by following the R4 §1.10 citation.

The 'In-box trace' Infra Prerequisites row names DF2.5 in the Lifecycle-Hook-Verified column though DF2.5 is not a predecessor; the scenario is out of scope for this story's e2e and DF2.5 is a downstream consumer, so no dependency edge is actually implied.
The UsageBreakdown semantics (input excludes cache reads, reasoning nested under output) appear in Technical Notes and the DoD Contract item but have no dedicated AC.
